role.altitude: From building pay scales, job profiles and reports by hand in Excel to owning a reward system: a maintained job architecture linked to CAO grades, a pay-equity model on the AFAS extract, and rules that flag exceptions. The specialist designs and checks that system and explains it to managers and the works council.
reach: Pay-equity and gender pay gap reporting under the EU Pay Transparency Directive, together with the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst
Personnel cost scenarios for the budget, which today the FP&A Analysts build
Checking flex worker rates on staffing agency invoices against CAO pay scales (inlenersbeloning), with the Bookkeepers
Drafting job profiles and pay ranges for vacancies, for the Recruiters
Pay checks before month close, alongside the Payroll Specialist
Training content on reward and appraisal, with the Learning and Development Specialists
role.ceiling_note: About 330 hours a year (roughly 21% of the role) are in these tasks, and maybe 120 to 150 of them can be saved. The limits are the works council's right of consent on pay and appraisal systems (art. 27 WOR), CAO grading rules that need human interpretation, AVG rules on salary and personal data, and the EU AI Act, which treats AI used to evaluate or promote workers as high-risk. Talks with managers, the OR and employees stay human work.
skills_to_grow: Power BI and DAX modelling on the AFAS extract
Writing and testing prompts and checks for Microsoft 365 Copilot
Pay-equity statistics (gender pay gap explained and unexplained)
EU Pay Transparency Directive and EU AI Act obligations for HR
Job evaluation methods used in Dutch CAOs (function grading systems)
Explaining models and trade-offs to the works council
role.ambitious_version: Every one of the roughly 1,200 roles, including flex roles, sits in one maintained job architecture with CAO grade, pay range, required certificates (Studytube) and career paths. A monthly pay-equity and pay-compression check runs on its own, and managers get scenario-based pay advice for each offer and promotion within a day. Noordhaven publishes its pay-transparency report early and with no surprises.

tasks.short: Design and improve how we pick, promote, pay, appraise and train people, and explain it to managers.

today.trigger: Annual HR planning cycle, a CAO change, or a problem raised by an HR Business Partner or the OR
steps: Collect current policies from SharePoint and data from AFAS and Recruitee
Benchmark against CAO rules and market information
Draft a method or policy change in Word
Discuss with the HR Director, HRBPs and the works council
Communicate to managers via Teams and intranet
drudgery: Finding the current version of policies
Rebuilding the same Excel analysis each year
Rewriting the same text for different audiences
today.time_sinks: Gathering scattered data and rewriting drafts after each review round.

lenses.faster: Copilot pulls current policies and AFAS figures into a first draft, so the gathering and first-draft steps shrink to an hour.
lenses.autonomous: A CAO update or a new Power BI trend (e.g. promotion rates by site) triggers a short briefing note with policies likely affected.
lenses.ambitious: Each method (promotion, appraisal, pay) gets a yearly evidence check on whether it predicts 90-day retention and performance, which is done properly for the first time.
lenses.joy: No more hunting for policy versions; the time goes to discussing trade-offs with managers.
lenses.options: Three to five policy variants with modelled cost and effect per site, instead of one proposal.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns a policy library with linked data and review rules, and checks what the drafts propose.
reach: Promotion and appraisal design with HR Business Partners
Training plan input for L&D

tasks.human_edge: Judging what is fair and workable on a shop floor in Venlo versus an office in Rotterdam, and getting the OR to agree.
tasks.pattern_why: The work is judgement and negotiation; AI helps with research, drafts and options, but the person leads.

in_practice.trigger: Policy review due date in the HR calendar, or a CAO change
steps: Copilot compiles current policy, CAO clauses and AFAS/Power BI figures into a briefing
Specialist sets the question and constraints
AI drafts two to four variants with cost estimates
Specialist edits and selects; HR Director and OR review
AI drafts manager and employee communication from the final version
in_practice.human_gate: HR Director sign-off and works council consent (art. 27 WOR) before any change takes effect
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint policy library with version history

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot drafts Word documents from SharePoint files
Policy variants with cost estimates can be drafted by an LLM from structured data

risks: Drafts copy outdated CAO clauses
Variants look precise but rest on weak data
OR sees AI involvement as a reason for distrust
research_questions: How many policy changes per year does the specialist actually drive, and how long does each take?
Is the SharePoint policy library current enough for Copilot to use?
Does the OR accept AI-drafted variants as input for consultation?

tasks.short: Run the appraisal cycle and equal-pay and equal-treatment programmes, and check whether they work.

today.trigger: Yearly appraisal cycle and the gender pay gap reporting obligation
steps: Prepare appraisal forms and timelines with HRBPs
Chase managers for completed appraisals
Export ratings and pay from AFAS to Excel
Analyse rating spread and pay differences by gender, site and grade
Report findings to the HR Director and OR
today.time_sinks: Chasing completion and cleaning data before any analysis can start.

lenses.faster: A Power BI model on the nightly AFAS extract calculates completion, rating spread and pay gaps, so the export-and-clean steps disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Reminders go out automatically to managers with open appraisals; a monthly pay-gap check flags groups over the 5% threshold of the EU Pay Transparency Directive.
lenses.ambitious: Pay equity is checked every month per site and grade, not once a year, and gaps are fixed before they reach the report.
lenses.joy: No more spreadsheet cleaning and chasing; the work becomes explaining gaps and fixing them with HRBPs.
lenses.options: Scenarios for closing a gap: cost per scenario over one, two or three years.
lenses.altitude: The specialist designs the equity model and its thresholds and reviews its exceptions.
reach: Pay transparency reporting with the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst
Appraisal process admin for HR Administrators

tasks.human_edge: Explaining why a gap exists, deciding whether it is justified, and handling sensitive talks with managers and the OR.
tasks.pattern_why: Pay-gap and completion metrics follow fixed formulas on structured AFAS data; no model is needed to run them.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract refresh and appraisal cycle dates
steps: Power BI computes completion rates, rating distribution and pay gaps by category
Power Automate sends reminders to managers with open appraisals
Flags appear for gaps above threshold or skewed ratings
Specialist investigates flagged groups and proposes action
Report to HR Director and OR
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist and HR Director review every flag before action; OR sees the yearly report
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI report history and an action log in SharePoint

evidence.claim: Power BI dashboards on AFAS data are standard practice
EU Pay Transparency Directive requires gender pay gap reporting and joint assessment above 5% unexplained gap

risks: Small groups make individual pay visible (AVG)
Wrong category definitions give misleading gaps
Automated reminders annoy managers if timing is off
research_questions: Does the AFAS extract contain all pay components needed for the directive's definitions?
How large are the comparison groups per site and grade after splitting?
When does Dutch implementing law set the first reporting date for a company of 1,200?

tasks.short: Keep personnel files and the employee handbook up to date in AFAS and SharePoint.

today.trigger: Contract change, CAO update, new policy, or audit finding
steps: Check AFAS records for missing or wrong fields
Update contract and pay data in AFAS
Edit handbook sections in Word on SharePoint
Check consistency with CAO and contract templates
Publish and notify staff
drudgery: Finding every handbook section a change affects
Keeping Dutch and English versions in step
today.time_sinks: Spotting inconsistencies between AFAS, templates and the handbook.

lenses.faster: Rule checks on AFAS find missing or inconsistent fields, and an LLM lists handbook sections affected by a change, so the manual search disappears.
lenses.autonomous: A weekly data-quality run flags records (e.g. contract end dates, CAO grade outside range) without anyone asking.
lenses.ambitious: A handbook that is always current, in Dutch, English and Polish for warehouse staff, with a Q&A in Teams.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses field-by-field checking; what is left is deciding wording and fixing real errors.
lenses.options: Two or three wordings for a handbook change, plain-language and formal.
lenses.altitude: The specialist maintains the rule set and the handbook source, and approves changes.
reach: Record quality checks now done by HR Administrators
Employee questions on pay and benefits

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what a policy change means for staff and getting the wording right legally.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps across AFAS and SharePoint with exceptions; a person must approve changes to records and the handbook.

in_practice.trigger: Weekly schedule, or a new CAO or policy file in SharePoint
steps: Rule checks run on the AFAS extract and list exceptions
LLM compares the change against handbook sections and drafts redlines
Drafts translated into English and Polish
Specialist approves record fixes and handbook edits
Published version notified via Teams
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves every record correction and handbook change before publishing
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS change log and SharePoint version history

evidence.claim: Copilot in Word can summarise and redraft documents
Rule-based data quality checks on HR extracts are routine

risks: Translation errors in legal wording
Sending personnel data to tools outside the AVG agreement
Agent writes to AFAS without proper approval
research_questions: What share of AFAS records currently fail basic consistency checks?
Which languages do warehouse staff actually need?
Does the Microsoft 365 tenant setup meet AVG requirements for personnel data?

tasks.short: Make org charts, career path overviews and pay analysis reports for management.

today.trigger: Management request, budget cycle, or yearly pay review
steps: Export headcount, grades and pay from AFAS
Build tables and charts in Excel
Draw org charts in PowerPoint or Visio
Write a short summary
Send to HR Director and managers
drudgery: Redrawing org charts after each change
today.time_sinks: Rebuilding charts and tables that change little from year to year.

lenses.faster: Power BI pages generate org charts, grade spread and compa-ratios from the AFAS extract, and Copilot writes the summary text.
lenses.autonomous: Reports refresh nightly; a monthly summary goes to the HR Director automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Every manager has a live view of their team's grades, pay position and career steps, instead of a yearly PDF.
lenses.joy: No more slide formatting; time goes to reading the numbers and what they mean.
lenses.options: Several cuts of the same data (by site, function family, shift vs office) without extra effort.
lenses.altitude: The specialist designs the report model and checks its numbers, rather than making reports.
reach: Personnel cost reporting for FP&A
Headcount reporting for the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst

tasks.human_edge: Choosing which numbers matter and what to say about them to a particular manager.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured AFAS data, fixed calculations, checkable output; a summary text can be an LLM step on top.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS refresh and monthly schedule
steps: Power BI model computes headcount, grade spread, compa-ratio, org structure
Row-level security limits each manager to own team
Copilot drafts a short narrative of changes
Specialist reviews the narrative and exceptions monthly
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist checks the narrative and unusual figures before distribution
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI workspace and report distribution log

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI drafts narrative summaries of report pages
Power BI with row-level security on HR data is standard

risks: Reporting lines in AFAS out of date
Salary data visible to the wrong manager
Narrative states causes the data does not support
research_questions: Are reporting lines in AFAS accurate enough to draw org charts?
Which managers would use a live view, and which still want a PDF?
Does the People Analytics analyst already own a model that this should reuse?

tasks.short: Research what jobs require, how jobs relate, and trends in logistics work and pay.

today.trigger: New role, regrading request, CAO negotiations, or market shortage
steps: Read CAO job descriptions and grading tables
Collect market data and salary surveys
Talk to managers and staff about the job
Write findings in a memo
drudgery: Comparing job descriptions line by line
today.time_sinks: Collecting and comparing sources by hand.

lenses.faster: An LLM summarises CAO texts, vacancy texts and surveys into a comparison table, so reading time drops sharply.
lenses.autonomous: A quarterly scan of logistics vacancy and pay trends lands in the specialist's inbox.
lenses.ambitious: Each job family has an up-to-date profile of tasks, skills, certificates and market pay, used by recruiting and L&D.
lenses.joy: Less reading of dense documents, more time with managers on the floor.
lenses.options: Several possible job family structures compared side by side.
lenses.altitude: The specialist curates the job knowledge base and checks the AI's comparisons.
reach: Job profiles for Recruiters
Skills and certificate needs for L&D

tasks.human_edge: Observing the real work in the warehouse and judging what a job actually demands.
tasks.pattern_why: Research is open-ended; AI speeds reading and comparison, the person checks and concludes.

in_practice.trigger: Regrading request or quarterly trend review
steps: Specialist states the question
Copilot or a research assistant summarises CAO, survey and vacancy sources with citations
Specialist checks sources and adds interview findings
AI drafts the memo; specialist finalises
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist verifies every cited source before the memo is used

evidence.claim: LLMs can summarise and compare documents with citations
Trend scans from public vacancy data are feasible

risks: Made-up or wrong market figures
Licensed survey data uploaded where the licence forbids it
research_questions: Which salary surveys does Noordhaven license, and do they allow AI processing?
How often do regrading requests come in per year?
Do managers trust AI-summarised trend notes?

tasks.short: Decide which job analysis tools we need and build questionnaires and interview guides.

today.trigger: New job family, regrading wave, or CAO grading change
steps: Review existing questionnaires and guides
Draft new questionnaire items in Word or Forms
Test with a few managers
Adjust and roll out
today.time_sinks: Drafting items and processing open-text answers.

lenses.faster: An LLM drafts questionnaire items mapped to the CAO grading factors and codes open answers into those factors.
lenses.autonomous: Open answers from Forms are coded automatically and the specialist sees a summary per job.
lenses.ambitious: Job analysis covers every job family, including flex roles, instead of only disputed ones.
lenses.joy: No more hand-coding of answers; time goes to testing whether the questions work.
lenses.options: Several versions of an instrument (short for shift workers, longer for office) to test.
lenses.altitude: The specialist designs the instrument family and checks coding quality.
reach: Survey design support for People Analytics

tasks.human_edge: Knowing whether a question makes sense to a forklift driver on a night shift.
tasks.pattern_why: Turning open answers into structured grading factors is unstructured-to-structured work inside a fixed process.

steps: LLM drafts items per grading factor
Specialist edits and pilots with managers
Forms collects answers
LLM codes open answers into factors with a confidence score
Specialist reviews low-confidence codes
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves the instrument and checks a sample of coded answers
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint job analysis folder with coded data

evidence.claim: LLMs can classify open text into given categories

risks: Coding errors move a job into the wrong grade
Questions not understood by non-native Dutch speakers
research_questions: Does the CAO grading system prescribe its own instrument?
How accurate is LLM coding against a hand-coded sample?
How many job analyses a year are needed?

tasks.short: Analyse workforce and sector data and give figures to management, CAO partners and government.

today.trigger: Request from management, CBS survey, sector body, or CAO talks
steps: Gather AFAS data and sector figures
Analyse in Excel
Write a note or fill in the form
Send and answer follow-up questions
drudgery: Re-doing similar extracts for each request

lenses.faster: Standard measures sit ready in Power BI, and Copilot drafts the note, so most requests take an hour, not a day.
lenses.autonomous: Recurring external surveys get pre-filled from the data model for the specialist to check.
lenses.ambitious: Management gets a quarterly reward and workforce brief with sector comparison, which does not exist today.
lenses.joy: No repeated extracts; the interesting part, explaining patterns, remains.
lenses.options: Several views and scenarios (e.g. wage increase options in CAO talks) costed quickly.
lenses.altitude: The specialist maintains the measure set and answers questions from it.
reach: Wage cost scenarios for FP&A during CAO talks
Data requests usually sent to the HRIS Analyst

tasks.human_edge: Knowing what a figure will be used for and what not to share.
tasks.pattern_why: Requests vary; AI speeds analysis and drafting but the person judges meaning and disclosure.

steps: Specialist records the request
Copilot queries the Power BI model and drafts tables and text
Specialist checks figures and disclosure
Send and log
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves every figure that leaves the company

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI answers questions about a semantic model

risks: Wrong figures sent to external parties
Personal data leaks through small numbers
research_questions: How many such requests come in per year, and from whom?
Is the Power BI model well documented enough for Copilot to query reliably?
Which external surveys recur?

tasks.short: Build and give training on pay, appraisal and benefits for managers and HR colleagues.

today.trigger: New pay policy, appraisal cycle, or new managers
steps: Write slides and handouts in PowerPoint
Plan sessions with L&D
Give training on site or in Teams
Collect feedback
drudgery: Scheduling across three sites and shifts
today.time_sinks: Rebuilding material and repeating the same session per site.

lenses.faster: Copilot turns the current policy into slides, a quiz and a short Studytube module, so material prep drops by half.
lenses.autonomous: New managers in AFAS are enrolled in the Studytube module automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Every manager can practise a pay or appraisal conversation with an AI role-play before the real one.
lenses.joy: Less slide work, more live discussion of real cases.
lenses.options: Short, long and on-the-floor versions of the same training.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the curriculum and checks content, with L&D running delivery.
reach: Module building usually done by L&D

tasks.human_edge: Live sessions where managers raise awkward cases and need a trusted answer.
tasks.pattern_why: Content drafting speeds up a lot; delivery and trust stay with the person.

in_practice.trigger: Policy change or new manager in AFAS
steps: Copilot drafts slides, quiz and module text from policy
Specialist checks and adds cases
L&D publishes in Studytube
Auto-enrol new managers
Specialist runs live Q&A sessions
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves all content before publishing

evidence.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint creates presentations from a Word document

risks: Out-of-date policy in training
Managers rely on the module instead of asking HR
research_questions: Does Studytube support automatic enrolment from AFAS at Noordhaven?
How many managers need this training per year?
Do managers want role-play practice, and does the OR agree to it?
